23: Hands fitting map pieces together: fragments that never close into a whole.
Letter blocks scattered on a table: the clues stay heterogeneous.
Tenement fronts: like the projects in Brooklyn's Finest, a situation read in pieces.
Two men in suits on a tenement street: plain-clothes watch, meaning withheld.
The street seen from the elevated railway: partial evidence from above.
24: An armoured truck and its guard: Metro Manila's van, the job that has itself become the problem.
A man in profile beside a logic machine: thinking takes the place of acting.
A black hole blasted in rock: a cipher at the centre of the world.
Workers amid excavation rubble: a world of problems no single act resolves.
25: A kaleidoscope: an optical sign announcing that we have entered another regime.
A distorted, stretched close-up: the image bends into dream.
Glowing spheres floating in black: a dream space set clearly apart.
A cartoon thought-cloud: the dream bubble, clearly bracketed off from waking.
A smear of blurred motion: the device that marks the passage into dream.
26: A gaunt worker at a machine in low light: the lathe of The Machinist, waking life already dreamlike.
A cup blurred at the edge of focus: the everyday slightly off.
A man dozing in an armchair: we can't tell when sleep began.
A woman opening a door onto darkness: an unmarked passage between worlds.
A hand with a cigarette against black: an isolated detail oddly insisted upon.
A dim window onto a blank wall: realism gone uncanny.
27: Coney Island rides at night: the world itself spinning in light.
Berlin's city machine in motion: the world moves with dream logic.
A chorus line on a lit stage: the musical where the décor dances, Deleuze's movement of world.
An animated swirl: the setting animates itself.
Skyscrapers slanting overhead: the city folding, as in Inception's Paris.
A lantern floating through an animated night: a dream with no dreamer to wake.
28: An older man in an armchair, lost in reverie: the moment before the flashback.
A bleached, overexposed march: the past visibly marked as past.
Hands holding old photographs: the recollection that will decide what happens.
A figure at a desk in lamplight: like the writer at the typewriter in The Secret in Their Eyes, the past pulling on the present.
A man lying back, eyes closed: memory about to take command.
29: A lone figure on a dirt road through dry land: Maria's road in White Material, the past colouring every step.
A colonial house and its veranda: a history hanging over the present without explaining it.
Figures walking through tall grass: transit through a landscape charged with the past.
A truck on a tree-lined road: movement suspended, destination uncertain.
An old, worn street scene: a fragment of the past that belongs to no one.
A crowded streetcar: bodies in transit, carrying histories no flashback explains.
30: A boy and his image in a hand mirror: the self doubled, each image an alternative.
Tracks forking at a station: paths literally branching.
A ship alone at sea: Triangle's liner, the same voyage coming round again.
A boat half-lost in fog: which crossing is this?
Two faces mirroring each other: the double within one frame.
A lone figure on a beach at dusk: Triangle's shore, where the loop restarts.
31: Identical row houses: repetition makes the relation visible.
Rows of cartridges: the series as a habit of the eye.
A planned street of matching houses: a pattern the viewer learns.
Glowing bulbs in a row: a series whose term is the single unit.
A printed list: Se7en's lists, the series written down.
A clerk at his ledger: the habitual entry, one more in the series.
32: A crop-duster low over a field: Deleuze's demark, a plane dusting where there are no crops (North by Northwest).
A windmill: Hitchcock's mill turning against the wind, the natural series broken (Foreign Correspondent).
Rows of identical figures with one singled out: the aberration drawn as a diagram.
A line of marchers with one figure out of place.
A creature coiled where it should not be: the snake in Buried's coffin.
A flock with a stray: the series shows its rule by breaking it.
33: A lighter held in the dark: Buried's flame, an object carrying the film's ideas.
A hand turning a key: Hitchcock's key, a relation made into an object.
A padlock and chain: bondage as an idea you can hold.
A gramophone horn: voice and memory cast in brass.
A wristwatch in close-up: time as an object.
A packed suitcase: departure thought through a thing.
